text:
maya: Quick Q — preparing a latency deep-dive for next week's infra review. Where's the canonical place to look for TTFT (time-to-first-token) + tokens/sec across models? Need p50/p95/p99 numbers, example PromQL for panels, and a pointer to traces/logs for slow requests. Anyone?

jonah: Start with the Grafana "Inference / Latency Overview" dashboard. Key panels: TTFT by model (panel id ~42), TTFT distribution (histogram), tokens/sec (panel ~58). Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/latency/inference-overview

jonah: Example PromQL I use for p50/p95/p99 (replace job/model labels):
```
# TTFT p50/p95/p99 (ms) for successful responses
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(inference_ttft_bucket{job="inference",status="ok",model=~".*"}[5m])) by (le, model)) * 1000
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_ttft_bucket{job="inference",status="ok",model=~".*"}[5m])) by (le, model)) * 1000
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_ttft_bucket{job="inference",status="ok",model=~".*"}[5m])) by (le, model)) * 1000

# Tokens/sec per replica
sum(rate(inference_tokens_generated_total{job="inference",model=~".*"}[1m])) by (model,instance)
```

ana: Also check the "tokenflow" dashboard for prefix-cache hits and tokens/sec breakdown by customer/route. If you want raw logs, use Kibana and this Lucene filter: `service.keyword:inference AND span.kind:server AND response.first_token_time: *` then inspect `response.first_token_time` and `request.sequence_length`.

ana: For traces: Jaeger samples are linked from the Grafana panels (open a slow TTFT trace -> click through to Jaeger). Quick Jaeger query: `service=inference AND operation=Generate` + tag `first_token_time>500` to find slow-start traces.

sre-bot: Alert notice: `TTFT_P95_HIGH` currently fires when p95 > 800ms for seq<1024. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/ttft-p95. Consider raising to 1s for large-batch jobs or adding exclusion on model=experimental.

josh: If you need a single Prom dashboard panel that shows p50/p95/p99 side-by-side, use a PromQL row with three queries (as jonah posted) and apply `legend {{model}}`. For tokens/sec, we usually switch to a 1m rate and stack by instance to catch noisy replicas.

maya: For Private deployments — are the metric names identical? I don't want to accidentally use the hosted-only metrics.

jonah: Yes, metric names are the same for Private/VPC deployments. Filter by `deployment_type="private"` or `tenant=<tenant-id>` in PromQL. Note: some private installs have lower scrape resolution (30s) so bump your rate window: `rate(...[2m])`.

maya: Cool. One more: any tips to distinguish model cold-start vs KV cache miss vs network hiccup in the trace?

ana: Good Q. Pattern matching:
- Cold-start: span timeline shows a long `container.init` or `process.start` before model load.
- KV cache miss: look for a long `kv.fetch` span and low `cache.hit` tag.
- Network hiccup: downstream span latency but no heavy CPU on GPU spans; check `net.rtt` tag and instance-level network metrics.

maya: Thanks — I'll assemble a short how-to for the review. Would appreciate one extra pair of eyes on the dashboard layout before I share. @josh @jonah can you skim?

josh: I'll take a look after lunch. :eyes:

jonah: Happy to. If you paste the Grafana snapshot link here I'll give feedback on panel ordering/labels.

maya: Snapshot: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/g/snapshot/abcd1234 — mainly TTFT by model, tokens/sec, histogram, and a trace quicklink panel.

josh: Looks good. Suggestion: add a small panel showing `prefix_cache_hit_ratio` so reviewers can correlate slow TTFTs with cache misses.

jonah: Also annotate the p95 alert threshold on the dashboard (visual line) and add a note about sequence-length segmentation (p95 for seq<128 vs seq>=128).

maya: Great, will update. thanks all! :thumbsup:
